name: Files
description: Store + sideload .appinstaller; MSIX install OS-Authenticode-gated, auto on launch.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Files supports Store updates and a sideload path using fixed HTTPS .appinstaller URLs. The sideload service compares the manifest package/version and delegates installation to Windows PackageManager; lifecycle code invokes update checks at startup and periodically. Windows Authenticode enforcement is an OS/package-deployment boundary outside this source review.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than historical release re-verification; Windows Store/package deployment signature enforcement, shipped MSIX metadata, and exact startup timing were not independently audited.

original_evidence.text: | Files (Store channel) | github.com/files-community/Files | WinUI 3, packaged MSIX | Y (`StoreUpdateService`, selected via DI when packaged and Store-associated) | Y — `AppLifecycleHelper.CheckAppUpdate()` runs automatically on every app launch (`App.xaml.cs:365`) and calls `CheckForUpdatesAsync()` + `DownloadMandatoryUpdatesAsync()` unconditionally; mandatory Store updates auto-download after a forced consent dialog, optional updates require the user to click Update in UI (`DownloadUpdatesAsync()`) | Y (`RequestDownloadAndInstallStorePackageUpdatesAsync`) | HTTPS, entirely inside the Windows Store client stack (`Windows.Services.Store.StoreContext`) — Files never talks to a URL itself | n/a (Store service, not a document manifest) | OS-code-signing — Microsoft Store re-signs/validates all packages via AppX Deployment Service before install; no app-level hash/signature check exists in this path | Microsoft Store signing infrastructure (root of trust is Windows' built-in trusted-app/Store certificates) | src/Files.App/Services/App/AppUpdateStoreService.cs:191 (`_storeContext ??= await Task.Run(StoreContext.GetDefault)`), :195 (`GetAppAndOptionalStorePackageUpdatesAsync`), :158 (`RequestDownloadAndInstallStorePackageUpdatesAsync`); src/Files.App/Helpers/Application/AppLifecycleHelper.cs:171-176 (`CheckAppUpdate`); src/Files.App/App.xaml.cs:365 |

| Files (Sideload/AppInstaller channel) | github.com/files-community/Files | WinUI 3, packaged MSIX via `.appinstaller` | Y (`SideloadUpdateService`) | Y for the version-check (runs on every launch via `CheckAppUpdate()`); download/install (`ApplyPackageUpdateAsync`) is user-triggered from UI, not silent | Y — `PackageManager.AddPackageByAppInstallerFileAsync` downloads and installs the MSIX package described by the `.appinstaller` XML | HTTPS — hardcoded URLs `https://cdn.files.community/files/stable/Files.Package.appinstaller` and `.../preview/...`; fetched with plain `HttpClient.GetStreamAsync` (default TLS cert validation, no pinning/overrides found) | N — the `.appinstaller` XML itself carries no signature; only package name + version fields are read (`XDocument.LoadAsync`) | OS-code-signing — `AddPackageByAppInstallerFileAsync` is a Windows AppX Deployment API that refuses to install any MSIX package whose Authenticode signature doesn't chain to a trusted publisher cert; Files' own code performs no hash/signature check itself | Publisher certificate embedded in the MSIX package's `AppxManifest`, validated by Windows against the local trusted-people/trusted-publisher cert store (external to the app) | src/Files.App/Services/App/AppUpdateSideloadService.cs:19-20 (URL consts), :90 (`_client.GetStreamAsync`), :215-217 (`new Uri(...)` → `AddPackageByAppInstallerFileAsync`) |
